title: Portable genus-1 smalljac and ffpoly
objective: Port the Sage.js smalljac/ffpoly accelerator to portable fixed-width arithmetic, native Windows clang-cl, macOS arm64, and Linux arm64 while retaining exact fallback and performance evidence

oracles: current Linux x64 smalljac coefficient stream

handoff.summary: Ports the exact genus-1 smalljac_Lpolys source closure and ffpoly word arithmetic to fixed-width types across Unix and native Windows. The portable arithmetic layer uses compiler-native 128-bit arithmetic where available and clang-cl intrinsics plus exact normalized division on Windows; fixed-width GMP adapters preserve LLP64 values. A checked source transformation and PowerShell clang-cl build install smalljac, ffpoly, and headers through build-deps.cjs. Optimized x86 remains the default where supported. Exact coefficient traces through prime 100000 agree across optimized Linux, forced-portable Linux, and native Windows for two representative elliptic curves; focused arithmetic tests also pass on Linux arm64 and Apple Silicon.
risks: The native addon and binding.gyp are shared integration files outside this lane. They must adopt the fixed int64_t/uint64_t callback ABI and enable/link the new Windows artifacts before Sage.js exposes smalljac on Windows.

End-to-end smalljac behavior for an individual prime above 2^32 was not performance-validated; the Windows GMP adapters independently pass exact boundary tests, while the analytic-rank coefficient intervals exercised here are exact through prime 100000.

The selected genus-1 closure deliberately omits STgroups.c and smalljac_moments.c because they implement the unrelated Sato-Tate moments API and are unreachable from smalljac_Lpolys. Upstream compilation still emits non-fatal empty-loop and deprecated strcpy warnings.
next_steps: Merge the branch tip and update packages/flint/src/addon.c callbacks and statuses from long/unsigned long to int64_t/uint64_t.
Broaden packages/flint/binding.gyp smalljac capability enablement and link smalljac.lib and ff_poly.lib on Windows, then run the integrated analytic-rank suite on all four CI platforms.
Keep high-prime Windows performance as a later optimization target if a caller needs individual primes beyond the analytic-rank coefficient range.
